items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: Because I brought Guy from Baton Rouge too and knew all of them to play with me at the entertainers club.

ctx.x: Did they have your name up? You know, did they advertise you were playing there as guest artist? No. No.

No, they didn't even advertise. Not as I can remember. But anyway, uh, this guy, Charlie Crest was playing, uh, accordion with Faith, the us at that time. And, uh, he got back to St. Louis. He had his own band. And, uh, he said for me to come up there, but I didn't go that time. Uh, because I had too much work in the owners. I couldn't leave. I mean, I had too many contracts signed. I couldn't leave. So, uh, so about six, eight months after he come down here, with Faith again, and the farm and then told me he had…
What did you, uh, you got any questions?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: And Guy Kelly coming in that night, and Guy and I played a number two with us.

ctx.x: Did they have many New Orleans grounds up there with those phones?

No. Uh, Gishard, he's from here, but he was playing with another band on the name of Eddie. Eddie something they was playing. He's a saxophone player too, a how-to player. And he had a brother, a dead shawty, played bass, but I think the young ones did the bass play. I think he died. I had a fellow out at, uh, Shreveport with, uh, Goldstone's band. I played a lot of, a lot of, a lot of Tramon too. A little skinny fella. I forget his name too. Fine Tramon player. I only had a guy playing trumpet there, second…
What were the names of the other people?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: And that's where I sent for Guy Kelly, trumpet player. Sent for him. And he come down there.

ctx.x: Where was that? No, it was in Baton Rouge. Oh. No, it was in Baton Rouge.

Then I stayed with Toody Harris about a year. Eight months a year. I got a telegram that my wife fixed to be operated on on a Saturday. And I got the telegram that Friday evening. And that's when I left that Friday evening. Come here. And uh... That Monday I went to work at the humming board. No, I played at the entertainers. I played at the entertainers for about six, eight months. And then we left there and... I went to the humming board. And that's where I sent for Guy Kelly, trumpet player. Sent for him. And…
I didn't think I wanted to go. I was doing alright there by the hummingbird. But anyway...
